newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea 1st qtr trade deficit seen at $7.4-$8 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea 1st qtr trade deficit seen at $7.4-$8 bln.

text.p: South Korea is expected to run a trade deficit of between $7.4 billion and $8 billion in the first quarter of this year, Trade, Industry and Energy Minister Ahn Kang-koo said in a television interview on Thursday.
But Ahn said during the interview with Yonhap Television News that the target for this year's deficit, set at about $14 billion, was still attainable.
The "trade deficit in the first quarter will be about $8 billion unless efforts are made and between $7.4 billion and $7.5 billion if efforts are made," Ahn said.
South Korea posted a customs-cleared trade deficit of $4.16 billion during the first quarter of 1996.
Last week, the ministry announced a record monthly trade deficit of $3.48 billion for January, compared with a $2.13 billion shortfall a year earlier.
"When taking into account past trends, our earlier estimate for this year is attainable without a big problem," said Ahn.

South Korea lost hundreds of millions of dollars in exports from nearly a month of strikes in most manufacturing industries. The strikes erupted in late December in protest at the forced passage of a new labour law.
The ministry has targeted narrowing this year's annual trade deficit to about $14 billion from a $20.38 billion shortfall in 1996.
